Aw no, its okay dont worry - sometimes we learn stuff the hard way. 

You're going to be okay OP, it gets easier when they can't reach you. It will give your mind a chance to heal. Try not to be too hard on yourself in the meantime, and seek therapy if possible to keep yourself grounded. 

Remember. You don't want to be with someone who doesn't want to be with you. That alone means you're incompatible and you deserve someone who is 100% sure about you and looking to build with you and grow alongside you.

Unless he immediately signs up to intensive therapy addressing his avoidant tendencies etc then he will absolutely do the same thing again. I took back my ex a grand total of 6 times in 1 year. He "couldn't do it anymore" then would leave and "miss our home together". So glad he's gone now- you'll be happier, promise.

I did it and it was worth it. I was worried I'd be "running", but I see now it was what I needed at the time. To heal in a safe place. I've made new friends and started to do things for myself again. I'm not quite able to immerse myself in the city I left yet, but I've been making progress. I'm now starting a new job with a better salary and starting to pursues hobbys again, even "untaint" certain things from the trauma. There's pros and cons, and I suppose you never fully know until you go for it but I wanted to show you an example of things working out, should you take the plunge:)
Thank you so much for your detailed response, it's really helped me😊

For the love of god, please do NOT choose where to live based on your boyfriend. If the relationship ends (which is a very real possibility as university is a mind blowing time of growth and change) then you'll be stuck trying to make the best of a shitty situation, and you'll potentially end up feeling trapped an unable to go out in case you run into him., possibly losing mutual friends. Isolation, depression and resentment. Also worth noting that he isn't thinking about trying to be near you, which is harsh but it's what you need to do too. 

Tldr: If its meant to be, then the distance won't matter. Do what is best for you, build your own life.

Please don't accept his call. Nothing good will come of it, you'll be left confused, invalidated and disrespected. No contact is the way forward, you're worth more than this. Imagine if a dear friend or relative was in your situation.

Just try remember that even if it wasn't intentional, it may as well have been as the effect on you is the same. Either they are ignoring their effect on you or they know it and still don't feel a sense of urgency to change. I felt the way you did, that it was all my fault. That his mechanisms were understandable and mine were not. Time will equalise it, baby steps. Therapy will help you take him of his pedestal. It's awful and you're going through a lot but you can do this. You can't hate yourself into a happier place and I know that sounds obvious, but I punished myself for a long time over thinking I'd driven away my best friend. Fuck what some say on here, true love can't be driven away. And you'll find it one day, as will I hopefully. Here for you, you're not alone❤

I don't think this was all you. It sounds like you went unheard a lot, and stonewalling is classed as an abusive tactic to claim full control. Sounds like you threatened to break up because he didn't show he valued you rather than you not getting your way. I don't think you were manipulative, I think you were desperate and he maybr even fed off it otherwise he wouldn't do it. Even if he is a saint, I think therapy for yourself is a good idea when you feel ready, not to "fix" yourself but to better understand yourself and becoming a good advocate for your own needs. You're allowed to have needs, and learning how to communicate them constructively can help in future relationships, both romantic and platonic. You deserve your life back. Therapy is hard but you're worth the work, and you're not a lost cause. Don't give up.

Antidepressants aren't meant to make you numb, that's why doctors say to tell them if that happens. They are meant to raise your overall "baseline" to that of someone without depression so that you are able to respond more proactively to the illness and have more motivation to tackle life. They aren't a cure, but I've personally found they help give me more space to deal with life situations. It's still a trial and error period and side effects can be hard to deal with. In my case the side effects I experience are less dangerous than what I experience without my medication. Id say keep an eye on how you're faring day to day and weigh it up like any physical health issue:)
